sofia torres: ran an nsys capture on staging with a prod-like mix (batch=8, seq=1024). seeing a big hotpath around attn_kv_lookup and some unexpected memcpy spikes. pasted top kernels from the summary below — full trace at https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234 :eyes:
```
Top kernels by GPU time:
1) attn_kv_lookup_kernel         42.3%  (grid=1024x32, block=256)
2) softmax_qk_kernel             18.1%
3) kv_cache_miss_handler         12.5%
4) cudaMemcpyAsync (D2H/H2D)    9.2%
5) rop_dispatch_kernel           7.8%
```
sofia torres: the odd thing is attn_kv_lookup is both high-time and low-occupancy in the timeline — looks like divergent warps on some branches. nvprof shows a lot of serializing calls around the cache miss path.
liam chen: can you paste the nsys summary (kernel args + grid/block)? low occupancy + high time usually points to either small warps or heavy register pressure. also: was this run with prefetch enabled?
sofia torres: prefetch=true by default in this config. I'll try toggling it. attached the nsys cmd I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --output=run_attn nsys.launch -- python ./bench_trace.py --config=staging_batch8
```
nina patel: looking at KV metrics in the server logs during that run — miss rate ~14% at batch=8 which aligns with more work hitting the miss handler. prefetch might be thrashing the cache on this sequence distribution. try cache_prefetch=false and run batch=4 and batch=8 to compare hit-rate + p50 latency.
omar reza: quick eyeball of the perfetto trace: there are repeated short cudaMemcpyAsync spikes that line up with logging flushes. those D2H syncs can serialize the stream. quick repro: run with logging level=warning and enable pinned host buffers for comms.
omar reza: command to try pinned mem: 
```
export REDWOOD_PINNED_HOST_BUFFERS=1
python ./bench_trace.py --config=staging_batch8 --no-verbose-logging
```
perf-bot: regression alert — attn_kv_lookup median time increased ~6% relative to baseline in build c3f9a7 (investigate recent changes to prefetch/kv eviction). CI: https://ci.internal/runs/98765 :warning:
liam chen: if we confirm miss_handler is the bottleneck, options: 1) fuse prefetch into attn kernel to avoid host-device roundtrips, 2) increase thread/block to improve occupancy, 3) add a lightweight bloom filter to avoid expensive miss-paths on common prefixes.
nina patel: I'll add a small experiment matrix in the ticket: batch sizes [4,8], prefetch [on,off], pinned_mem [on,off], measure: attn_kv_lookup time, KV hit%, overall p50/p95. assigning follow-ups: @omar reza to run pinned_mem test, @sofia torres to run prefetch=false variants. I'll update issue #233 with results.
sofia torres: thanks — I'll kick off three runs now and post the summaries (nsys summary + a small table) when done.
liam chen: one more thought — the softmax_qk_kernel looks heavier than expected vs prior traces; could be quant changes or fused ops falling back to slow path. check kernel name suffixes for quantized variants.
sofia torres: good call. will grep the kernel names for "qkv_quant" / "fused" and include that in the report.
omar reza: ping me if you want me to spin a perfetto capture with CPU stacks on, that helps reveal logging-induced syncs.
sofia torres: ack — will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
